$comment: GENERATED by scripts/units/year/type-work-list.js. Never edit by hand.

A.title: My five senses
A.differs: K-355 matches each object picture (a drum, a rose, a rainbow, a lemon, a feather) to the eye, ear, nose, tongue or hand picture, every sense once (level 1 four senses, level 2 all five), no words on the page. The real one-sense-at-a-time stations and the talk about smell and sight finding good food are the lesson's, not the page's.

A.title: Parts of my body
A.differs: K-354 copies six body words from a bank onto lanes that point to a drawn child (arm, leg, hand, foot, knee ...); K-363 circles every part we have two of; K-360 counts parts on the child's own body. No page asks which parts help us eat, drink and breathe.

A.title: Living or not living?
A.differs: Draw a line from each picture to Living or Non-living (cat, bird, frog, flower ... / chair, cup, rock, snowflake ...). There is no seed and no water on the page, so 'a seed is living, a rock and water are not' stays the lesson's talk.

A.title: Weather words and our weather chart
A.differs: K-364 is the week chart (draw the day's weather symbol in each box, Monday to Sunday); K-356 matches the six weather symbols to their words; K-365 reads a thermometer against a cold / warm / hot color key and circles the clothing that fits.

A.title: The four seasons
A.differs: K-322 sorts pictures into the four seasons, K-207 summer and winter clothes, K-338 names the season of three pictures, K-339 puts the seasons in order on the wheel, K-340 crosses out the odd one, K-341 draws the tree in each of the four seasons.

A.title: Where animals live
A.differs: K-204 sorts pets and wild animals, K-209 farm and wild animals (two groups each; no single three-group sort); K-383 draws a line from each animal to its home (bird and nest, bee and hive, spider and web, rabbit and burrow, ant and anthill, beaver and lodge).

A.unit: Sink, Float and Build a Boat
A.title: Sink or float? Test it
A.differs: K-384 draws two things that float on the water line and two that sink to the bottom; G1-399 (grade 1, pictures only, fits K) is the record of the real tub test: color a ring in the guess tank, then one in the test tank (ball, log, apple, leaf, feather, pencil / rock, nail, hammer, scissors, potato ...). A cork, a plastic lid and a marble are not in its bank; choosing boat materials is the next lessons' work.

A.title: What plants need to grow
A.differs: In each row circle the plant that gets both things it needs (the others miss water, light or both). The two-week drawings of the class seedlings in the window and the cupboard are not on a page.

A.title: Fruits and vegetables: food from plants
A.differs: Draw a line from each food to Fruits or Vegetables (the tomato kept a vegetable, the kitchen convention). That every one comes from a plant is the lesson's talk.

A.title: Animal babies and what they need
A.differs: Draw a line from each grown-up animal to its baby (cow and calf, hen and chick, horse and foal, sheep and lamb, duck and duckling, butterfly and caterpillar). What each baby needs (milk, seeds, leaves) is not on the page.

A.unit: Sunlight and Caring for Our Earth
A.title: Day and night
A.differs: Draw a line from each picture to Day or Night (sun, rainbow, kite, bird / star, owl, bat, comet). The Moon is left off, so looking for the Moon in the morning sky stays the lesson's.

A.unit: Sunlight and Caring for Our Earth
A.title: Natural or made by people?
A.differs: Draw a line from each picture to Natural or Man-made (flower, rock, leaf, mountain, sun / car, house, chair, book, cup). The group is printed 'Man-made', not 'made by people', and nothing shows people cutting trees for wood and paper.

A.unit: Sunlight and Caring for Our Earth
A.title: Recycle, reuse and keep Earth clean
A.differs: K-357 draws a line from each empty or finished product to its bin; K-366 circles the bin. The English bins are five material bins (paper and cardboard, plastic, glass, metal, compost) with no trash bin; reusing one thing and picking up litter are not on a page.

A.title: Our five senses
A.differs: G1-357 sorts pictures by sense, G1-358 circles the body part used, G1-359 crosses out the odd one, G1-360 writes each sense word next to its organ, G1-361 finishes 'I can hear ...', 'I can see ...' sentences.

A.unit: Sky Patterns: Weather, Sun, Moon and Stars
A.title: Weather words and the weekly forecast
A.differs: G1-362 writes each weather symbol's word in letter boxes; G1-363 reads a five-day forecast and circles the day for each question. Its questions only ask which day is sunny, rainy, snowy ...; 'the best day for outdoor recess' and 'the day that needs a raincoat' are the teacher's.

A.unit: Sky Patterns: Weather, Sun, Moon and Stars
A.title: Sun, Earth and Moon
A.differs: G1-378 checks each fact sentence under the Sun, the Earth or the Moon; G1-391 numbers moon pictures 1 to 5 as the Moon grows or shrinks.

A.title: Animal groups and body coverings
A.differs: G1-201 sorts animals into Mammals, Birds and Reptiles; G1-205 into Fur, Feathers and Scales. How each covering helps is the lesson's talk.

A.title: Parts of our body and their jobs
A.differs: Find each numbered part on the figure and write its name, one letter in each box. The jobs of the parts and the comparison with animal parts are not on the page.

A.title: Where animals live and what they need
A.differs: G1-398 writes the letter of each animal's habitat window; G1-202 draws lines to where animals live; G1-406 crosses out the animal that does not live in each habitat; G1-206 and G1-407 cover what animals eat.

A.title: Parts of a plant
A.differs: Follow each numbered tag to a part of the drawn plant (root, stem, leaf, flower, fruit, seed) and write its name from the bank. The jobs of the parts are on G2-364, not on this page.

A.title: Life cycles in order
A.differs: The chicken (G1-203, write 1 to 3), the butterfly (G1-377), the plant (G1-388, cut and glue from the seed) and the frog (G1-389, cut and glue round the pond); G1-390 circles what comes next for the butterfly, the frog and the ladybug.

A.unit: Materials: Sink, Float and Build a Raft
A.title: What is it made of?
A.differs: G1-364 writes what each thing is made of from the bank; G1-365 draws three things the family recycles and writes what each one is. Sorting the real clean recycling is the lesson's hands-on part.

A.unit: Materials: Sink, Float and Build a Raft
A.title: Sink or float? Predict and test
A.differs: G1-204 sorts objects into Float and Sink; G1-399 records a guess and then the test for each object (the apple, the pumpkin and a log float; a nail sinks); G1-408 circles the thing that floats on a balance scale (heavy things that float). Choosing raft materials is the next lesson's.

A.title: Sort by material
A.differs: G2-348 circles the one thing in each row made of a different material; G1-364 writes each thing's material from the bank (paper, plastic, glass, metal ...).

A.title: Floating facts: shape the clay
A.differs: G2-382 colors where a clay ball and a clay boat end up, circles what floats and draws an own clay boat; G2-383 circles true or false for floating facts.

A.unit: Earth Changes: Every Day, Fast and Slow
A.title: Why do we have day and night?
A.differs: Look where the Sun is and circle day or night at each numbered pin on the Earth. Turning the globe in the flashlight beam is the lesson's demonstration.

A.unit: Earth Changes: Every Day, Fast and Slow
A.title: The Moon's shapes in a month
A.differs: G2-367 writes the name of each moon (new moon, first quarter, full moon, last quarter) from a bank; G1-391 puts moons in their growing or shrinking order. Checking the chart against the real Moon is the lesson's.

A.title: Plant parts and the parts we eat
A.differs: G2-364 finds the part that does each job on a tagged plant; G2-363 circles the part of the plant we eat for each food.

A.title: Life cycles: from egg to grown-up
A.differs: G2-365 writes the four butterfly stage names under their pictures and crosses out the extra name; G2-366 puts each young stage (tadpole, caterpillar, chrysalis ...) under the animal it becomes.

A.title: Habitats and how animals adapt
A.differs: G2-380 writes the letter of the animal each adaptation sentence tells about (one left over); G2-381 is the habitat report: draw three animals and a plant in the habitat picture, write their names, circle the word that fits the habitat.

A.title: A fair test: one change at a time
A.differs: My Lab Report: choose a sink-or-float question, write a prediction, test it, draw what happened and write what was learned. The page does not name the one thing changed or the things kept the same.

A.title: The water cycle
A.differs: Write evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection on the numbered lines of the water-cycle diagram. The cup marked each day and the cold glass are the lesson's investigations.

A.title: Butterfly and frog life cycles compared
A.differs: Put a check under the butterfly, the frog or both for each sentence; 'every life cycle includes birth, growth, reproduction and death' is the lesson's summary.

A.title: Flowers make seeds
A.differs: Write the name of each numbered part of the flower (petal, sepal, stamen, pistil ...) and cross out the bank word that is not a part of a flower. Taking a real flower apart is the lesson's.

K-212.title: What does a body need to live?
K-212.differs: K-212 Wants and Needs draws a line from each picture to Needs or Wants (needs: water, apple, bread, shirt, house; wants: ball, doll, candy, television, balloon): a family's needs with clothes and a home, not what a body needs to stay alive, and no air (no child breathing). Change: a body-needs bank (food, water, air) with the circle-and-cross-out task; level 3's drawing box is new.
K-212.note: a body-needs bank (food, water, air) with the circle-and-cross-out task; level 3's drawing box is new.

K-364.title: Wind watch
K-364.differs: K-364 keeps a week of daily weather in day boxes, but its six symbols (sun, cloud, rain, storm, snow, rainbow) have no wind, and nothing shows a streamer hanging, fluttering or flying out. Change: a wind face of the K-356 diary layout with three drawn streamer states to circle in each day box; level 3's windiest and calmest day circles are new.
K-364.note: a wind face of the K-356 diary layout with three drawn streamer states to circle in each day box; level 3's windiest and calmest day circles are new.

G1-407.title: What do animals eat?
G1-407.differs: G1-407 (grade 1, pictures, no animal names) circles for each animal the one food it eats of two and its home; G1-206 sorts animals into plant eaters and meat eaters (no 'eats both'). Nothing gives three food pictures per animal with two right for the bear and the robin, and nothing records what the class animal or the feeder birds ate. Change: an 'eats' face of the G1-398 habitats family with three food chips and omnivores.
G1-407.note: an 'eats' face of the G1-398 habitats family with three food chips and omnivores.

K-383.title: Animals change their world
K-383.differs: K-383 draws a line from six animals to the homes they make (nest, hive, web, burrow, anthill, beaver lodge), so the animal-to-what-it-made match exists; there are no before-and-after pairs showing the land changed (bare ground and an ant hill, a stream and a beaver dam), no squirrel hole and no schoolyard drawing. Change: a before/after face of the same pairs.
K-383.note: a before/after face of the same pairs.

K-511.title: Push or pull?
K-511.differs: K-511 level 2 sorts pictures into 'moves by itself' and 'needs a push or a pull' (a ball, a swing, a sled, a cart, a door ...): forces are named, but a push is never told apart from a pull and there are no action pictures (kicking a ball, pulling a wagon). Change: a push / pull rule with action pictures on the same science-category-sort layout (lines to a push hand and a pull hand).
K-511.note: a push / pull rule with action pictures on the same science-category-sort layout (lines to a push hand and a pull hand).

K-057.title: Shadows
K-057.differs: K-057 Match the Shadow (a line from each picture to its silhouette) is the need's level 1. Nothing draws the flashlight, the toy and its shadow on the wall, or compares the shadow of a toy near the light and far from it. Change: a two-box drawing level (near / far) with a circle for the bigger shadow and the sentence frame.
K-057.note: a two-box drawing level (near / far) with a circle for the bigger shadow and the sentence frame.

K-208.unit: Sky Patterns: Weather, Sun, Moon and Stars
K-208.title: Stars come out at night
K-208.differs: K-208 sorts sky pictures into Day and Night (sun, rainbow / star, comet ...), so the day sky and the night sky are told apart, but there are no two windows to draw in and nothing says the stars are still there in the day. Change: a two-window drawing face with a picture bank (the Sun, stars, the Moon allowed in either window) and the sentence frame.
K-208.note: a two-window drawing face with a picture bank (the Sun, stars, the Moon allowed in either window) and the sentence frame.

G3-334.unit: Sky Patterns: Weather, Sun, Moon and Stars
G3-334.title: How long is the day?
G3-334.differs: Bar graphs to color exist: G3-334 builds a bar graph from a value table, G1-481 colors one box per tally. Their categories are theme pictures (fruits, pets ...); there are no months along the bottom with hours of daylight up the side and no dashed prediction bar. Change: a daylight mode of the graph-tasks factory (months, hours 9 to 15).
G3-334.note: a daylight mode of the graph-tasks factory (months, hours 9 to 15).

G3-334.title: Our weather data: tables and graphs
G3-334.differs: G3-476 reads thermometers in degrees Fahrenheit (0 to 100) and G3-334 builds a bar graph from a value table, but no page holds weather data: daily highs, precipitation and clouds for ten school days, or a comparison with the fall. Change: a weather-data mode of the graph-tasks bar-fill (school days, highs in °F on a scaled axis) with the table and two comparison questions.
G3-334.note: a weather-data mode of the graph-tasks bar-fill (school days, highs in °F on a scaled axis) with the table and two comparison questions.

G3-334.title: What weather to expect each season
G3-334.differs: G3-334 builds a bar graph from a value table with theme pictures as the categories; no twelve-month climate table (average high in °F, inches of rain) and no season boxes to describe. Change: a monthly climate mode with the season boxes.
G3-334.note: a monthly climate mode with the season boxes.

G1-530.title: Make a map: land and water
G1-530.differs: G1-530 Draw Your Own Map (level 2 an island outline with a road and a river, key rows to fill) is the need's level 3; G1-379 reads a key on an island map. Nothing colors land and water from a color key or labels a lake, a river, a hill and the ocean from a word bank. Change: a land-and-water face of the maps family (color key boxes, a lake and hills on the island, four labels).
G1-530.note: a land-and-water face of the maps family (color key boxes, a lake and hills on the island, four labels).

G2-508.title: Globe toss: more water or land?
G2-508.differs: G2-508 is the same record for another experiment: numbered trial boxes, a tally for each outcome, the bars and a guess to compare (level 1 a bag of two kinds, 20 draws). Change: a globe-toss mode with two outcomes (water, land), 10 or 30 catches and the frame 'Most of Earth is covered by ___.'
G2-508.note: a globe-toss mode with two outcomes (water, land), 10 or 30 catches and the frame 'Most of Earth is covered by ___.'

G2-558.title: Can it change back? Make an argument
G2-558.differs: G2-558 Plan Your Opinion Piece has boxes and frames for an opinion, reasons and a closing on school-life questions: the shape of an argument, not a science claim backed by what was seen in a test. Change: a claim / evidence mode ('My claim: ___ can / cannot change back.' 'My evidence: I saw ___.' and a drawing box) with the unit's changes as the questions.
G2-558.note: a claim / evidence mode ('My claim: ___ can / cannot change back.' 'My evidence: I saw ___.' and a drawing box) with the unit's changes as the questions.

G1-481.title: Schoolyard survey: how many kinds?
G1-481.differs: G1-481 has the record this survey needs, a tally line per picture and an empty bar graph to color (its bug list has ant, spider, snail, ladybug), but it is a favorites vote ('Ask 8 classmates'), one list, no plants (clover, grass, dandelion), no two habitats side by side and no count of kinds. Change: a field-survey mode with two side-by-side tallies and a two-bar graph of the kinds.
G1-481.note: a field-survey mode with two side-by-side tallies and a two-bar graph of the kinds.

G1-481.title: Hide and survive: camouflage
G1-481.differs: G1-481 is a tally line per choice and an empty bar graph, and its color list (red, blue, green, yellow ...) can name the moth colors, but it is a favorites vote: no two backgrounds, no table of moths found on each, no sentence frame. Change: a two-background tally table and bar graph for the camouflage game.
G1-481.note: a two-background tally table and bar graph for the camouflage game.

G2-381.title: Compare habitats: desert, rain forest, ocean
G2-381.differs: G2-381 draws three animals and a plant into ONE habitat picture and names them; nothing compares three habitats in columns or counts the kinds. Change: a three-column chart face of the habitats family (desert, rain forest, ocean) with a picture bank for level 1.
G2-381.note: a three-column chart face of the habitats family (desert, rain forest, ocean) with a picture bank for level 1.

G2-380.title: Plants for every habitat
G2-380.differs: G2-380 matches adaptation sentences to animals; the habitats family has no plants (no cactus, fern or water plant cards). Change: a plant face (three plants, three habitat windows, the helping part to circle) on the G1-398 habitats layout.
G2-380.note: a plant face (three plants, three habitat windows, the helping part to circle) on the G1-398 habitats layout.

D.title: Rain gauge: how much rain fell?
D.differs: No rain gauge or water-level record exists. Build cups with tape marks to color up to the mark and a circle for the day with more rain, from the measuring-cup drawing of G2-260 and the day boxes of K-364.

D.title: Getting ready for a storm
D.differs: K-365 reads a cold / warm / hot thermometer and circles the clothing that fits (scarf, T-shirt, sunglasses): the 'what to wear tomorrow' part only. No page has a thunderstorm, a tornado warning or a snowstorm with safe choices (go indoors, the safe room). Far: a storm-safety face (a weather picture and three drawn choices per row, circle the safe one) on the row layout of K-365 or the choice rows of G1-404.
D.note: a storm-safety face (a weather picture and three drawn choices per row, circle the safe one) on the row layout of K-365 or the choice rows of G1-404.

D.title: Build a home for an animal
D.differs: G1-407 circles each animal's food and home and G2-381 draws animals into one habitat picture, but nothing has the child build a place for one animal from cut-outs (food, water, a place to hide), and the habitats family never draws water. Far: a cut-and-glue habitat model page (an empty place box, a strip of eight cut-outs, two that do not fit) on the cut-and-paste layout of G1-388.
D.note: a cut-and-glue habitat model page (an empty place box, a strip of eight cut-outs, two that do not fit) on the cut-and-paste layout of G1-388.

D.title: A harder push, a farther roll
D.differs: No push investigation record exists. Build a start-line strip with gentle / medium / hard rows (an arrow to color, the ball drawn where it stopped, floor tiles counted); the test rows of G1-399 are the closest record layout.

D.title: Change its direction
D.differs: No page shows a ball changing direction after a push. Build four pictures (a wall, a bat, a hand, a slanted block) with two arrows to circle (level 1) or an arrow to draw.

D.title: Make the ball hit the target
D.differs: No engineering design page exists (draw the ramp, circle 'it worked' or 'try again', show the change). Build it as an open record with pictures of the changes to circle for level 1.

D.title: Which ramp works better?
D.differs: No page compares two designs by their test results. Build two ramp pictures with three tally boxes each and a circle for the better ramp; the trial boxes and tally of G2-508 are the closest layout.

D.unit: Sink, Float and Build a Boat
D.title: Draw a boat for the bear
D.differs: G2-382 ends with 'draw your own clay boat in the big tank' after testing a clay ball and a clay boat, the only boat-design drawing; there is no bear, no strip of materials to circle and no ready boat outline for level 1. Far: a boat-plan face of the G1-399 sink-or-float family (the bear in a box, a material strip, a big drawing tank, label words for level 3).
D.note: a boat-plan face of the G1-399 sink-or-float family (the bear in a box, a material strip, a big drawing tank, label words for level 3).

D.unit: Sink, Float and Build a Boat
D.title: Build and test our boats
D.differs: No page records a boat test (my boat / after the test, a dry or a wet bear, one change). Build it on the tank drawings of G1-399 and G2-382.

D.unit: Sink, Float and Build a Boat
D.title: Which boat carried more?
D.differs: No load test exists. Build a flat raft and a boat with sides, each with a row of 10 or 20 penny circles to color one by one (the frame coloring of K-005 is the closest layout) and a circle for the boat that held more.

D.title: Plant a seed and watch it grow
D.differs: No seed journal exists. K-341 (draw the same tree in four seasons) is the closest layout, four frames to draw one thing over time: build four boxes with a dashed clear-cup outline, a day line, taller / the same to circle and a leaf count.

D.unit: Sunlight and Caring for Our Earth
D.title: Sun or shade: which is warmer?
D.differs: No sun-and-shade comparison exists. Build pairs of pictures (a cup of water, a rock, sand, an ice cube) in the sun and in the shade, the warmer colored red and the cooler blue; level 3's thermometers can use the thermometer drawing of K-365.

D.unit: Sunlight and Caring for Our Earth
D.title: Make shade for an ice cube
D.differs: No shade design page exists. Build materials to circle, a drawing of the shade over the ice cube and all / half / none of the ice to color after the test.

D.title: Feel the buzz: vibrations make sound
D.differs: No sound or vibration page exists. Build a four-station chart ('I felt it shake' / 'I saw it shake' to circle, the moving part to draw); the check-under-a-column table of G1-378 is the closest layout.

D.title: Sound makes things move
D.differs: No page records sound making things move. Build three before-and-after test rows with 'it moved' / 'it stayed still' to circle.

D.title: Cup telephones
D.differs: No cup telephone or other sound-device page exists. Build a plan box (circle the cups and string), a drawing and a three-row test chart ('I heard it' / 'I did not hear it').

D.title: We see only with light
D.differs: No light-and-seeing page exists. Build the two peep-box pictures (window closed, window open) with 'I saw it' / 'I did not see it', a drawing box each and the sentence frame.

D.title: Does light go through?
D.differs: No light test exists. Build one row per material and three icon columns (all light, some light, no light) to color after testing; the check-under-a-column tables of G1-378 and G3-393 are the closest layout.

D.title: Mirrors bounce light
D.differs: No mirror or light-path page exists. Build a room drawing with a flashlight, a mirror and a star (trace the dashed path; choose the mirror turned the right way; two mirrors).

D.title: Send a message with light
D.differs: No light-signal page exists. Build a flash-code key to fill, a drawing of the signal device and a three-message test chart (sent, received, right or wrong).

D.unit: Sky Patterns: Weather, Sun, Moon and Stars
D.title: My shadow through the day
D.differs: No shadow-through-the-day page exists. Build a stick with east and west marked and three Sun-and-shadow drawings (morning, near noon, afternoon) with a circle for the shortest shadow.

D.unit: Sky Patterns: Weather, Sun, Moon and Stars
D.title: Moon journal
D.differs: No moon journal exists. Build a month grid of empty circles to shade, with a picture key of the shapes for level 1, on the calendar grid of G1-524 with the moon drawings of G1-391.

D.title: Animal parents and their young
D.differs: No page shows what animal parents do for their young (K-205 only pairs a grown-up with its baby). Build four family pictures with action chips to circle (feeds, carries, keeps warm, protects / calls, follows) on the chip rows of G1-407.

D.title: Copy an animal: design a helper
D.differs: No design-from-nature page exists. Build a three-pair match of animal parts to inventions (turtle shell and helmet, webbed feet and flippers, beak and tongs) on the pair layout of K-205, then a drawing box and the sentence frame.

D.title: Like their parents, but not exactly
D.differs: No parent-and-young comparison exists (K-205 only pairs grown-ups with babies). Build parent and young picture pairs with clue words to circle (the same) or cross out (different) and the sentence frame; a gray cygnet and spotted puppies are new art.

D.title: Young plants and grown plants
D.differs: No seedling record exists. Build a drawing of the grown bean plant, three seedling boxes with a leaf count, and a same / different check table for leaf shape, size and color.

D.unit: Materials: Sink, Float and Build a Raft
D.title: Design a raft
D.differs: G2-382 ends with drawing an own clay boat in a big tank, the only design drawing for floating; no materials checklist, no labeled parts, no load of ten pennies. Far: a raft-design face of the G1-399 sink-or-float family (material pictures to check, a sketch box, three label lines).
D.note: a raft-design face of the G1-399 sink-or-float family (material pictures to check, a sketch box, three label lines).

D.unit: Materials: Sink, Float and Build a Raft
D.title: Test two rafts
D.differs: No two-design test record exists. Build two raft drawings with a tally and a total box each and 'one good thing' / 'one thing to fix' lines; the trial boxes and tally of G2-508 are the closest layout.

D.title: Describe it: hard, bendy, rough, soaks up water
D.differs: No property table exists. Build a materials-by-test table (hard or soft, bends or stays stiff, rough or smooth, soaks up water or not, icon-headed columns) to check, with a sort two ways; the check-under-a-column table of G3-393 is the closest layout.

D.title: The best material for the job
D.differs: No material-testing page exists. Build a data table (drops before it leaked, was the toy wet?), a bar chart to color (the bar-fill graph of G3-334 is the closest) and the claim line.

D.title: Take it apart, build something new
D.differs: No build-and-rebuild page exists. Build two drawing boxes with a piece-count line each and a same-count check.

D.title: Shape the land: a landform model
D.differs: K-377 matches things drawn from the side to the same things seen from above, the side-view / top-view move, but with furniture and objects, not landforms. Far: a model-to-map page (a side-view box and a top-down map box with a key; landform pictures to circle for level 1).
D.note: a model-to-map page (a side-view box and a top-down map box with a key; landform pictures to circle for level 1).

D.title: Where is water on Earth?
D.differs: No water-on-Earth sort exists. Build eight picture cards (ocean, river, lake, pond, glacier, iceberg, snowy peak, puddle) to glue into a two-by-two grid (solid or liquid, salty or fresh); the two-attribute sort of G1-485 is the closest layout.

D.unit: Earth Changes: Every Day, Fast and Slow
D.title: Fast changes: earthquakes, volcanoes, landslides
D.differs: No fast-or-slow Earth events page exists. Build eight event cards to glue on a two-part timeline (minutes, hours or days / many years); the cut-sort-glue layout of K-264 is the closest.

D.unit: Earth Changes: Every Day, Fast and Slow
D.title: Slow changes: water shapes the land
D.differs: No erosion record exists. Build before-and-after drawing boxes for the sand hill, a tally of the cups poured and three real-place photos to match.

D.unit: Earth Changes: Every Day, Fast and Slow
D.title: Stop the sand from washing away
D.differs: No design-comparison page exists. Build two design sketches with before / after hills, spoonful counts and a strength and a weakness for each.

D.unit: Earth Changes: Every Day, Fast and Slow
D.title: Which real solution is best?
D.differs: No solutions chart exists. Build four photo cards in a chart (stops wind or water?, how it works, one problem with it) with a star for the chosen one.

D.title: Where does ice melt fastest?
D.differs: No melting record exists. Build four places with boxes for 10, 20 and 30 minutes to color how much ice is left, and fastest / slowest to circle.

D.title: Melt it, freeze it back
D.differs: No heating-and-cooling record exists. Build three materials with before / warmed / cooled boxes and 'it changed back' / 'it did not' to circle.

D.title: Changes we cannot undo
D.differs: No reversible-change sort exists. Build six before-and-after picture pairs with 'can change back' / 'cannot change back' to circle; the picture-and-chips rows of G1-403 (circle before, during or after) are the closest layout.

D.title: Do plants need light and water?
D.differs: No plant investigation log exists (K-376 only circles the plant that gets light and water). Build a four-cup by three-week table (height in inches, leaf color, drawing), the conclusion frame and a bar graph of the final heights.

D.title: Seeds on the move
D.differs: No seed-dispersal page exists. Build the fur-model box, a six-seed 'stuck / fell off' chart and a three-way sort (sticks to fur, eaten by animals, blown by the wind). G3-511's text 'How Animals Plant Trees' covers only the eaten seeds, at grade 3 reading level.

D.title: Be a pollinator
D.differs: No pollination page exists. Build a garden map of four flowers for the bee's path, flowers to color when they got pollen, and a label.

D.title: Balanced and unbalanced forces
D.differs: No force page exists. Build six pictures with force arrows to draw (matching or different lengths) and balanced / unbalanced, stays still / starts to move to circle.

D.title: Predict the swing
D.differs: No pendulum or motion-pattern page exists. Build a table of trials for each string length, a prediction line, a check line and a bar graph for level 3.

D.title: Friction slows it down
D.differs: No friction test exists. Build a surfaces-by-trials table with a median distance in inches, a bar graph to color (the bar-fill graph of G3-334 is the closest) and the sentence frame.

D.title: Balloon tricks: static electricity
D.differs: No static electricity page exists. Build four tests with prediction and result columns (moved toward, moved away, did not move) and the question line.

D.title: What do magnets pull?
D.differs: No magnet test exists. Build a twelve-object table (what it is made of, my prediction, result) and a pulled / not pulled sort; the guess-then-test rows of G1-399 are the closest record.

D.title: Magnet force from a distance
D.differs: No magnet-distance page exists. Build a ruler strip to mark where the clip started to move, a trials table for two magnets and a 'through it?' chart.

D.title: A problem magnets could solve
D.differs: No engineering problem planner exists. Build the problem / criteria / constraints frames with three illustrated problems and criteria to circle for level 1.

D.title: Design and compare magnet solutions
D.differs: No solution-scoring page exists. Build three sketch boxes, a criteria-by-solution check table and a test-result line.

D.title: Climates around the world
D.differs: No climate page exists. Build four place cards with small temperature and rainfall graphs, a world map to mark (the world map of G2-370) and a hot and dry / hot and wet / cold sort.

D.title: Define a weather problem
D.differs: No hazard planner exists. Build the hazard / problem / criteria / constraints frames with a sketch of the school and three illustrated hazards for level 1.

D.title: Which design reduces the damage?
D.differs: No hazard-test page exists. Build two design sketches, a results table and a claim-evidence-reasoning frame.

D.title: Raise mealworms through their life cycle
D.differs: No observation log exists. Build a dated table (drawing, length in inches, stage) and a circular beetle life-cycle model to complete; the round stage layouts of G1-377 and G1-388 are the closest.

D.title: Traits from parents
D.differs: No traits page exists. Build a set of two parent dogs and five puppies, a traits table and the two questions; the pictures are new art.

D.title: Traits the environment changes
D.differs: No inherited-or-environment page exists. Build two plant drawings with heights and leaf counts, the short dog text and a two-column sort of eight traits.

D.title: Animals in groups
D.differs: No group-living page exists. Build four animal cards with 'how the group works' / 'how it helps members survive' columns and a claim-evidence frame.

D.title: Survive well, less well or not at all
D.differs: No survive-well sort exists. Build a habitat card, eight living-thing cards that name their needs and three columns with because lines; the window-and-cards layout of G1-398 is the closest.

D.title: Fossils tell about long ago
D.differs: No fossil page exists. Build four fossil photo cards in a chart (what lived here, what the place was like then, what it is like now).

D.title: When a habitat changes
D.differs: No solution-judging page exists. Build the short text about the change, two solution cards, a helps / costs table and a claim frame.
